summary: The week's standout is a single decided mega-event — Cabinet's ₹52,878cr IDBI-Fairfax approval, India's largest financial-sector FDI — alongside a draft National Steel Policy and confirmed 8% 2027 steel demand growth that convert last week's framework into dated policy plus live pricing power. Data-centre capex keeps compounding (Hillhouse, Lightstorm) just as MeitY moves to regulate its power draw, copper producers' duty push creates a clean tailwind/headwind split against solar-module and cable makers, and Brent above $106 with Houthi escalation sharpens the refiner-margin-vs-protected-city-gas divide.

themes.name: IDBI Bank strategic sale to Fairfax
themes.thesis: Cabinet-approved sale of a 60.72% stake (govt 30.48% + LIC 30.24%) to Fairfax at ₹81/share, above the ₹75.99 fair-value benchmark, recapitalises and re-rates IDBI while LIC books a one-off divestment gain.

drivers.what: Cabinet approves Fairfax's ₹52,878 crore bid for 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank, India's largest financial-sector FDI

beneficiaries.mechanism: Direct recipient of a priced, decided ownership change at a premium to independent fair value; strategic owner replaces government overhang.
Monetises its 30.24% stake at a premium to carrying value, a one-off capital realisation.

themes.name: Steel capacity & import protection
themes.thesis: A draft National Steel Policy Vision 2047 (604 MT capacity target, AI-based substandard-import monitoring) lands alongside confirmed 8% 2027 demand growth and a third month of price hikes, converting last week's framework into a dated policy plus live pricing power for domestic mills.

drivers.what: Draft National Steel Policy proposes AI-supported monitoring to curb substandard steel imports, targets 604 MT capacity by 2047
India's steel demand to grow 8% in 2027, fastest among major markets; steel prices rise for third consecutive month

beneficiaries.mechanism: Demand growth and anti-dumping/AI-monitoring protection support domestic realisations.
Same demand and import-protection tailwind; stock already moved 6% on the news.
Stainless segment benefits from the same import-screening push against substandard imports.
Domestic alloy/steel maker benefits from pricing power and demand growth.
Integrated steel producer benefits from the same demand/price cycle.
Alloy steel maker rides the broader pricing recovery.

Integrated steel producer benefits from the same cycle.
Manganese/iron ore feeds expanding steel capacity.
Graphite electrode consumable demand scales with EAF/steel capacity expansion under the 604MT 2047 roadmap.
Refractories demand scales with steel capacity additions.

themes.name: Copper price rally & import-duty push
themes.thesis: Record-high global copper prices plus a producer lobby push to double the duty on solar PV copper ribbons/busbars (5%→10%) is a clean tailwind for the domestic copper miner and a cost headwind for every copper-intensive downstream maker (solar modules, wires/cables).

drivers.what: Primary copper producers' body urges government to retain/raise duty on copper used in solar modules, citing underutilised 30,000-tonne domestic capacity vs cheap imports
Copper's bullish momentum likely to continue for a few more months

beneficiaries.mechanism: Direct domestic copper producer benefits from both the price rally and a protective import duty on copper-intensive components.
Solar module maker's copper-ribbon/busbar input costs rise whether sourced domestically (producers want higher prices) or via a higher import duty.
Same copper-ribbon input-cost exposure as other solar module makers.
Same copper-ribbon input-cost exposure as other solar module makers.
Smaller-scale module maker faces the same input-cost pressure.
Copper is the dominant input cost for wire/cable makers; a sustained rally compresses margins unless fully passed through.
Same copper-cost pass-through risk as other cable makers.
Copper-intensive cable manufacturer faces margin risk from sustained price strength.

themes.name: Data centres & digital infrastructure
themes.thesis: Fresh hyperscale and fibre capital commitments (Hillhouse, Lightstorm) land the same week MeitY confirms it is drafting a national data-centre policy to manage grid impact — the capex cycle keeps outrunning the governance response, which itself signals the scale is now too large to ignore.

drivers.what: Hillhouse launches data centre platform TeraNova DC, may deploy $12-15 bn in India by 2032
Lightstorm bets $500 mn on fibre networks to tap India's AI data centre boom
Government drafting national data-centre policy after installed capacity projected to reach ~8GW by 2030, 17GW by 2031-32

beneficiaries.mechanism: Listed data-centre developer directly captures incremental hyperscale demand and capital inflow into the sector.
Server/HPC maker supplies compute hardware for new DC capacity build-out.
Optical fibre cable maker supplies the backbone connectivity new DC campuses need.
Fibre and optical networking gear maker benefits from Lightstorm-type fibre expansion.
Enterprise network/data-centre connectivity provider rides the same hyperscale demand.
DC cooling/HVAC equipment demand scales directly with new campus construction.
Power/EPC solutions provider for DC campus electrical infrastructure.

themes.name: Power transmission & grid capex
themes.thesis: NTPC's ₹17 lakh crore 10-year investment plan and a Cabinet move to extend the power transmission fund by 5 years keep the evacuation/transmission capex cycle flowing, following on from the Green Energy Corridor-III approval.

drivers.what: NTPC plans ₹17 lakh crore investment over 10 years to meet rising power demand
Cabinet nod sought to extend power fund for 5 years

beneficiaries.mechanism: Transmission/power cabling demand scales with the extended capex pipeline.
Transmission tower maker benefits from sustained grid capex.

themes.name: Renewables, solar & storage
themes.thesis: NTPC is actively seeking overseas buyers for green ammonia and low-carbon fuels (talks with Japan, Korea, Germany), extending India's renewables story from domestic capacity addition into an export business line.

drivers.what: NTPC seeks overseas buyers for green ammonia, low-carbon fuels; in talks with Japan, South Korea, Germany for green fuel exports

beneficiaries.mechanism: Direct beneficiary of NTPC's green ammonia/low-carbon export push, opening a new revenue line beyond domestic power.

themes.name: Crude/LNG security vs. refining margins
themes.thesis: Brent above $106 as Houthi attacks on Saudi targets intensify squeezes refiner/marketer margins even as the government explicitly shields city-gas users from the Hormuz-driven LNG shock — widening last week's gap between upstream realisations and downstream margin pressure.

drivers.what: Brent crude rises above $106 as Houthis intensify attacks on Saudi targets
India shields city gas users as Hormuz crisis threatens South Asia's LNG demand

beneficiaries.mechanism: Upstream producer captures higher crude realisations as Brent rallies past $106.
City-gas distributor explicitly shielded from the Hormuz-driven LNG cost/supply shock.
Same government protection of city-gas allocation during the Hormuz crisis.

themes.name: Financial market infrastructure
themes.thesis: A dense run of SEBI circulars this week — notified common ad code, notified PMS/PRIM rules, SME IPO reform, extended IPO-size relaxation to March 2027 — deepens primary-market activity that RTAs, depositories and brokers all monetise through volume.

drivers.what: SEBI notifies common ad code for market intermediaries, allows celebrity endorsements
SEBI notifies PMS rules, introduces PRIM route, broadens portfolio-manager investment avenues
SEBI plans sweeping SME IPO rule changes, raises profit threshold to ₹3 crore; extends IPO issue-size relaxation to March 2027

beneficiaries.mechanism: Depository revenue scales with IPO count and demat-account growth from a sustained primary-market boom.
RTA volumes benefit from expanded PMS/AIF activity and SME IPO flow.

themes.name: Textiles & apparel PLI
themes.thesis: India says the first phase of the US trade deal is finalised, with legal drafting ongoing — a tariff-relief tailwind for US-facing apparel exporters, though Goyal's own phrasing keeps the operational benefit conditional for now.

drivers.what: India says first phase of US trade deal finalised
Legal drafting on in US trade pact; to be operationalised once we get competitive advantage: Goyal

themes.name: Defence & aerospace
themes.thesis: Four separate decisions in one week — ₹2,400cr MSME/startup procurement, a MoD commitment to a 15-year drone/counter-drone roadmap, GE Aerospace doubling India supply-chain spend to $400mn by 2030, and the Fleet Support Ship-1 delivery — move this from sentiment to multi-channel order flow.

MoD to give defence industry 15-year outlook on drones, counter-drone systems
GE Aerospace to boost India supply chain spending to $400 million by 2030, eyes more component sourcing
